explanation: Persistent strengthening of synapses via high-frequency co-activation of pre- and postsynaptic neurons, driving AMPA receptor insertion.
Requires both presynaptic glutamate binding and postsynaptic depolarization to expel Mg²⁺ ions, enabling Ca²⁺ influx.
Activated by Ca²⁺/calmodulin to phosphorylate AMPA receptors and promote trafficking of new AMPA channels to the PSD.
Canonical declarative memory pathway linking recurrent CA3 associative networks to CA1 output neurons.
Sustains late-phase LTP (L-LTP) for hours to days by upregulating plasticity-related proteins including BDNF.
Gradual reorganization during slow-wave sleep ripples transferring memory index dependencies from hippocampus to neocortex.
Sparse neuronal subpopulations active during encoding whose reactivation is sufficient to drive conditioned recall.
Low-frequency stimulation producing modest Ca²⁺ rises that activate phosphatases (calcineurin) and internalize AMPA receptors.
Fast ionotropic Na⁺/K⁺ channels mediating routine excitatory postsynaptic potentials (EPSPs); surface density increases during LTP.
Weakly stimulated synapses set local structural tags that capture plasticity-related proteins synthesized via separate strong L-LTP events.
E-LTP lasts 1–3 hours via kinase phosphorylation alone, whereas L-LTP persists beyond 24 hours and requires new transcription and translation.
Primary cortical input gateway into the hippocampal trisynaptic circuit, projecting from entorhinal cortex to dentate granule cells.
Projects from dentate granule cells to CA3 pyramidal neurons; expresses an NMDA-independent, presynaptic cAMP/PKA-driven form of LTP.
Sparse firing across numerous dentate granule cells orthogonalizes overlapping sensory inputs into distinct memory representations.
Dense recurrent autoassociative collaterals among CA3 pyramidal neurons reconstruct complete stored patterns from partial retrieval cues.

concept: Hippocampal Place Cells & Entorhinal Grid Cells
explanation: Spatial navigation neurons firing at specific environmental locations (CA1/CA3 place cells) or periodic hexagonal lattices (medial entorhinal grid cells).
High-frequency (150–250 Hz) oscillatory bursts during slow-wave sleep and quiet rest that replay waking neural sequences for consolidation.
Millisecond-scale Hebbian rule: presynaptic spikes arriving shortly before postsynaptic firing induce LTP, while reversed timing induces LTD.
Reactivating a consolidated memory temporarily returns it to a labile, protein-synthesis-dependent state where it can be updated or disrupted.
LTP drives actin polymerization that enlarges mushroom spine heads and postsynaptic densities (PSDs), stabilizing newly inserted AMPA receptors.
Medial temporal lobe and hippocampus encode explicit facts and events, whereas basal ganglia (striatum) and cerebellum store implicit motor skills and habits.
Dorsolateral prefrontal cortex (dlPFC) recurrent microcircuits sustain task-relevant information online across brief delays without long-term synaptic storage.
Postsynaptically generated diffusible signals (nitric oxide in LTP; endocannabinoids in DSI/LTD) traveling backward to modulate presynaptic release.

concept: Patient H.M. & Medial Temporal Lobe Amnesia
explanation: Bilateral medial temporal lobe resection caused profound anterograde declarative amnesia while sparing working memory, procedural learning, and remote memories.
